data.title: Agile sprint flow with agent input
data.summary: Sprint planning today is manual: edit mockdata.js#sprints[] by hand. Goal: agents PROPOSE sprint compositions based on plan ROI/effort/blockers/milestone; humans accept/override. The proposal + acceptance flow needs a clear data model and a UI on sprint.html.

sections.body: sprints[] in mockdata.js carries id, theme, starts, ends, status, items[] (slugs). project.html surfaces the activeSprint as a kanban preview; sprint.html shows the full board. There's no agent-proposed flow — sprint composition is hand-edited.

New verb: /plan-sprint propose [N]. Agent reads inventory + per-plan ROI/effort/blockers/milestone + last activity. Builds a candidate sprint with proposed_by:'agent/opus' and agent_rationale[] (one line per item). Writes to sprints[] with status:'planned'. sprint.html renders proposed sprints distinctly, with a 'Lock' button that flips status to 'active'.

Once a sprint is active, humans can /plan-sprint move <slug> <to-sprint> to relocate items. Each move appends to overrides[] with timestamp + reason. The sprint.html UI shows agent rationale as a tooltip on each item and visually distinguishes human-moved items.

decisions_def.title: When do agents propose sprints?
decisions_def.context: Three cadences: (a) on-demand — only when human runs /plan-sprint propose, (b) scheduled — weekly (cron skill?), (c) continuous — every agent that finishes work re-evaluates and may post a proposal note.

decisions_def.title: Where does agent rationale per item live?
decisions_def.context: Each proposed sprint item carries a why_now field. Options: (a) sprint.items[].why_now (item-scoped), (b) sprint.proposals[] array indexed by proposal_id (multiple proposals tracked), (c) per-plan field on the inventory.

decisions_def.title: How do humans accept/reject a sprint proposal?
decisions_def.context: Proposal status is 'planned'. To make 'active': (a) a Lock button on sprint.html — single-click flips status, (b) /plan-sprint start <id> from CLI, (c) edit mockdata.js by hand. The Lock button is the tight-loop UX but adds a JS handler + POST.

sprint-proposal-cadence.rationale: implement with the claude api - this would be a great use of a weekly task

agent-rationale-location.rationale: what do you recomend? the why now seems fragile. proposal or justification is stronger. per-item should probaly be scoped per item

proposal-acceptance-ux.rationale: we should be able to select sprints / switch between them. the agents should have access (easy access) to this sprint data

notes.body: Recommendation on agent-rationale-location (still open): keep per-item, but RENAME the field from `why_now` to `justification`. `why_now` is fragile (a question); `justification` is a stronger noun and matches the agile vocabulary (justification for inclusion in the sprint). Per-item scoping is what you asked for. To lock: click the per-item chip + add a rationale; the rename will land as a small schema patch when implementation begins.

followups.title: Resolve the three decisions on this plan; then update plan-sprint SKILL.md
followups.body: Once cadence, rationale-location, and acceptance-UX are locked, update ~/.claude/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md and add Lock button to sprint.html. Update mockdata.js (or its successor schema) to carry the new sprint fields.
